utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All the accused are here. All Defence teams that I can see. Prosecution, I note, is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye, and I don't think there is anyone behind the column. So before we continue with Ms. Frease's testimony, there is one pending motion, Prosecution motion that we told you we would be deciding orally. Here is our decision: The Trial Chamber is seized of a Prosecution motion for leave to amend witness list by adding one intercept operator supervisor, Witness 196, as a 92 ter witness and for protective measures. This motion was filed on the 16th of February. It was followed by a response on behalf of Drago Nikolic, filed on the 21st of February, and subsequently by a Popovic Defence motion, basically joining the Nikolic response in its entirety. All these three instruments, filings were filed confidentially. We will not be mentioning any names so we can proceed in public. By means of the motion, the Prosecution proposes to call Witness 186 pursuant to Rule 92 ter and also seeks an order of protection pursuant to Rule 75 in relation to this witness, allowing the assignment of a pseudonym and the use of facial distortion during his testimony. So basically the request is for the Trial Chamber to grant the Prosecution's request to amend the 65 ter list of witnesses and permit the appearance and testimony of Witness 186, and in addition that this witness be granted the protective measures I referred to before. In their response the Drago Nikolic and the Vujadin Popovic Defence teams raise various objections to the Prosecution motion. I'm going to deal with them one by one and decide them as we go along. The first objection is in the sense that the additional witness proposed by the Prosecution is not the operator who transcribed the intercept dated 19th January 1995. That is P2437. As such, the Defence submits that calling this witness would defeat the Trial Chamber's 12th September, 2006 decision on Prosecution's motion to admit written evidence in lieu of viva voce testimony pursuant to Rule 92 bis. Our decision is as follows: The argument that the additional witness proposed by the Prosecution is not the operator who transcribed the intercept dated 19th January 1995 in itself is not a fundamental reason, a basic reason why consequently the Prosecution motion should be dismissed. In addition, the Trial Chamber has taken into account the argument or the reason brought forward by the Prosecution, namely that in regard to this particular intercept -- intercept, they have been unable to identify the operator/transcriber of the intercept itself. As a result of this we are of the opinion that -- or we come to the conclusion that the Defence argument does not hold water. The second objection is in the sense that the Prosecution motion is filed out of time and that the Trial Chamber's 12 September, 2006 decision should not be read as a blanket decision to call additional intercept witnesses at any time during the Prosecution case. Admittedly we cannot agree more with the Defence objection or statement that our 12th September, 2006 decision should not be read as a blanket authorisation, and this is precisely why in each case that the Prosecution wishes to add to the 65 ter witness list, as far as intercept operators are concerned, as well as others, permission is to be sought. And the Trial Chamber will grant or dismiss according to circumstances. In this case the Prosecution has sought permission. We have still not closed the chapter on intercept evidence, and that in itself is not a determining factor, but we cannot agree with the Defence assertion that the Prosecution motion is filed out of time. And then there are three objections that we are going to put in one basket, namely, the intercept in question falls outside the temporal scope of the indictment, to wit in the sense that it deals with -- supposedly was intercepted in January of 1995. Additionally the intercept does not involve the acts or conduct of one or more of the accused in the context of the charges laid against the accused. And finally that the Prosecution, according to the Defence, has not shown that this intercept is critical to the Trial Chamber's understanding and determination of the issues raised by the indictment. This objection can be summarily dismissed by reference to our prior decision of the 10th of January 2007, during which dealing with exactly the same intercept we had stated that it is prima facie relevant and probative of issues raised in the indictment. It would be superfluous to repeat the arguments and submissions and details of our decision. So, in conclusion, there being no arguments brought forward to sustain -- no arguments brought forward contesting the justification issuing the protective measures sought by the Prosecution, our decision is to grant the Prosecution motion in total. This witness will be assigned a pseudonym and he will be Witness PW-158, and he will testify in addition with the protective measures of face distortion. The Prosecution is of course granted leave to include this witness in its 65 ter witness list. All right. Later on, Mr. McCloskey, we would like to have a word with Mr. Nicholls in relation to the matters that were raised yesterday. We need to know what his position is now, after having had the opportunity to go through the redacted versions of the two documents to -- which Mr. Bourgon and Mr. Zivanovic referred to yesterday so that we would be put in a position to decide the matter. So I suggest after the break or at the beginning of the next session. So -- yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. We -- I did indeed show the redacted versions to my colleague yesterday, who was -- said that he does not agree and does not want to entertain these documents being admitted as such in the redacted form. Now, with respect to these specific documents, having reviewed the matter and having reviewed the testimony of that witness on both Thursday and Friday of last week, we are of the view that we do not need to file these documents in evidence, whether in redacted or in a non-redacted form, as we believe that the credibility of the accused, what we wanted to do, has been done. So it is not necessary. That being -- that being said, Mr. President, the issue however, in itself is bound to come up once again. And to us it is very important that whenever it's an issue of credibility and whenever it's an issue of filing a document for impeachment purposes, our view is first that the Prosecution should not be involved in the process. The Prosecution should not decide what the Defence wants to file in evidence to impeach a witness. That's the first part of the equation. And the second part of the equation is, we are of the view that only those specific portions should be -- that the document itself should be redacted in order to show just a specific portions of the documents -- of the document that are necessary for impeachment purposes. And it appears to us, Mr. President, that this is also in line with a previous rule of the Trial Chamber if not a ruling at least an opinion which was given and I, with all due respect, refer the Trial Chamber to page 856 of the trial record at lines 15 to 18 where this issue was previously discussed. It appears to us now that the Trial Chamber would be changing view by asking for all the documents to be admitted in evidence. Now, of course in this case it doesn't apply; we simply withdraw and we do not want these two documents admitted. But it is an issue that is bound to come up again, if there are other witnesses that -- for whom we wish to file documents for impeachment purposes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. I take it that then Mr. Zivanovic's submission becomes moot?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. All right. So I think there is no further business to discuss on this. Judge Kwon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, could you give me the date of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I believe, Judge, 28th of August of this year. 28 August of 2006, sorry. And page 856 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- lines 15 to 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was in a different context, Mr. Bourgon, and we never of course relinquished our prerogative to ask for an entire statement to be produced nonetheless if we so deem it necessary in the interests of justice and for our better understanding of the proceedings. But in any case, we'll -- we'll come to that matter whenever it arises again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. My apologies to you, Ms. Frease. I knew that you would bear with us, but between standing outside in your room, waiting to be called and not knowing at least you have had the pleasure of assisting to this part of the proceedings. So we are going to continue and finish with your examination-in-chief, and then we will proceed with the cross-examination. As it looks for the time being, on paper, I don't think we will finish with your cross-examination today. But the chance is slight -- a slim chance is there. So let's start with the examination-in-chief, Mr. Vanderpuye. Let's continue with the examination-in-chief. Hope we don't start it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Frease.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Fortunately I only have a few questions left for you. If I could just have Madam Usher for one moment, please. I would just like to show the witness these two packets that I think have been provided to the Defence. And also to the Court. Now, Ms. Frease, you testified yesterday about two identified intercept operators who had not been called in the Prosecution's case, and I wondered if you had had an opportunity to see these packets before?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do those packets relate respectively to those intercept operators?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity to look at the contents of the packet, that is the underlying intercepts themselves?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And those intercepts, were they included as part of the Prosecution's collection of intercepts?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were they derived from notebooks obtained by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you observe anything about those intercepts, having reviewed them, that suggests to you that they were created in any manner differently from any of the other intercepts you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, can you tell me, tell the Court rather, that in your review of the intercepts that form the collection that the Prosecution has put forward in this case, did you ever come across one that was done in a way or contained information such that it caused you to have serious questions about the authenticity or reliability of the intercept collection as a whole?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. That concludes my direct examination. Thank you very much, Ms. Frease.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. Who is going first? Mr. Zivanovic, how long do you expect -- I know that we have a fresh estimate, but maybe if you declare it ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked for two hours, and I believe that this is exactly how much I will need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will have as much time as you require for the time being, provided you don't ask repetitive questions. So go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Ms. Frease.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You've told us that you started working in the Prosecutor's office of this Tribunal in April 1995 and that you started working on the intercepts sometime in March or April 1998. Do you know whether the Prosecutor's office, before 1998, asked from the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina to be provided with these intercepts? So did this happen before 1998, at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what kind of replies did you get from the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, if any, and if you know that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I vaguely remember a request in the fall of 1997 that the Office of the Prosecutor made to the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, to which I believe we did not receive a response, and which we followed up on in January of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that already in 1995 that there was a request for these intercepts?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had heard that intercepts existed, but I'm not aware of a formal request having been made at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about informal requests?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get any response to any of those informal requests?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: My memory is that the responses were essentially that the timing wasn't right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever approach the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina during that period of time, between 1995 and 1998, and asked them to explain that bad timing? Did you ask for an explanation of that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself didn't. Whether someone in the Office of the Prosecutor did, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you yourself not interested in the reasons for the delay? Did you not want to know why the intercepts were only submitted three years later and not before?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were involved in a lot of other activities, and it wasn't an area that was my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And whose responsibility was it? Could you tell me that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The team leader, Jean-Rene Ruez.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You were supposed to evaluate the authenticity of these intercepts. The fact that these intercepts were not provided to you for as long as three years, did it have any relevance in the assessment of the authenticity of these intercepts?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the possibility that these intercepts might have been fabricated, reinvented, corrected, and tampered with during that period of three years?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically during that period of three years, but that that was a possibility in general, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: During the three-year period, do you know where the material surrounding these intercepts was? Where was it physically located?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where it was found only.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where, where was it found?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was found at the northern site. A collection of the notebooks were found at the northern site. And some of the tapes were found, were located at the 2 Corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what about the printed material, where was that found?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the 2 Corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what about floppies, disks?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were provided to us by staff members of the 2 Corps from their records there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The floppies followed the notebooks with a one-year delay. Did you ask why?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you simply not interested or did it just not occur to you that you should ask? Did you just forget to ask?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a process, and as we learned more about the process, it then became relevant to ask for -- to ask whether they had the electronic copies of those recordings. At the beginning it was all very new, we were learning the process as we went along.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that -- that you did not request all of the material from them at once, that you just asked for some piecemeal deliveries?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was very sensitive material to them. And it required building trust among the OTP team and the people that we were working with in Tuzla. So we went -- we went by -- step by step and as that trust developed and as we learned the process, more material was given to us, including those diskettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, in 1998 you received just some of the material as a result of the limited trust that the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina placed in you at the time. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that trust was a factor, and I also -- let me say that it wasn't clear to us what was necessary in order to understand the full process.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the process of transcribing intercepted conversations, the transfer of transcribed conversations on to other bodies, is that what you mean when you say "process"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could just ask you to clarify what you mean, "on to other bodies."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Certain institutions within the BiH army, certain units that followed a certain hierarchal organisation. For example, a unit from northern site would inform its superior command and the latter would then contact their superior command in turn. This is what I meant when I said "other bodies."

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998, were you told what the process was? Who was it who informed whom about those intercepted conversations and how the communication was carried out?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was members of 2 Corps staff that began to inform members of the Office of the Prosecutor's team.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you informed at the time about the line that those intercepts follow from the moment the conversations were intercepted onwards to the higher, to the superior commands? Did you know it at the time? Did somebody tell you exactly what the chain was?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean were we -- were we told whether the conversations were forwarded to the command at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that as well. But I suppose that you were told what the purpose was of interception and who should be informed about those intercepted conversations within the military structures of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were told that they were sent to headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 you were provided with some tapes, a certain number of tapes, you were provided with notebooks and you were given a binder containing some 550 pages all together, as you say. You could conclude, based on all that, what the -- what methodology was used to intercept conversations. My impression is that no further explanation was necessary, that you could have inferred from all that what was necessary in order to intercept and process those conversations. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Then can you explain what the case was, what would be a fair representation of your knowledge at the time?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- I think to come back to an example that we've used in the past, the fact that two or three conversations were recorded at the same time. We didn't know that there were multiple units working at a particular site when we started, so it required more investigation to understand how the entire process worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You say when you started working. What period exactly do you have in mind? Is it the time when you started working on intercepts, sometime in March or April? Is that the time that you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did it take you to acquire that knowledge that you have just talked about, to learn about the process?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we gained a -- I gained a much better understanding once we started to interview the operators, which was in 1999. So it took over a year, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And before that you were never told that the conversations were recorded at various places, not just one place?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Exhibit number 1D226.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have it before you?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report dated 24 April 1998. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we scroll down a little, please? It says here, "Results of investigation." And in the first paragraph it says, "On 21 April 1994" - it says here 1994 but I believe it was 1998 and that this is just a typo - that the gentleman in question went to the northern site, and that together with him was Ms. Stefanie Frease. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we please move to page 3? Page 3 of the document. Could you please look at the fifth paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we not have English translation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Has this been translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The original is in English. The translation is into B/C/S. The original is English, I'm sure of that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The only document in the system is this one in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but if it's being made use of, we will need it in English. Yes, Madam Fauveau first.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may assist the Chamber, the same document is in the system under number 5D187, and there is indeed a translation into English available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No comment, Your Honour, anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So perhaps we can see it. We need to be able to follow. I mean, and I can't follow in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is there a concern about names of certain participants?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No one has mentioned this, but let's go into private session for a short while, yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, I conclude based on this that you were aware of the existence of both of these sites when you started working on intercepts. Is this fair to say?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I had an opportunity to see that the last batch of materials that arrived concerned the printed versions of the intercepts and that this arrived in the Tribunal in 2001 in the month of January. As far as I understand, at the time you no longer worked for the Tribunal. But given your subsequent engagement, I'm sure that you are aware of that batch of material that arrived at the time?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me which batch of material you are referring to and who would have brought it in? Whether it was printed or electronic versions?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Goes to the electronic version -- I correct myself, the typed or printed versions. That material was mentioned in the statement of Jean-Rene Ruez. I cannot tell you or be more specific about the material because in his statement he said that it was reams of materials that was being recorded when he was given the statement and that was in March 2001. And out of that statement it follows that no other printed materials had been received by the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that. I recall there being electronic material that was brought in by Jean Gagnon, and I believe that was at the beginning of 2001, and that Jean-Rene Ruez had brought material in, in December of 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look together, please, at the statement that I just mentioned by Jean-Rene Ruez. It's Exhibit from the Prosecution list, P1087 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could counsel repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you repeat the number again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you could repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. P1079. Correction, P1079, not P1087. Yes, now it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is Jean-Rene Ruez's declaration. Could we take a look at the next page, please. At the bottom there is the date 10th of March, 2001. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's peruse the last paragraph of that declaration, for starters. There is mention being made of a mass of printed transcripts, and it is said that they were transferred to the OTP in January 2001, and that they are being listed or registered.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about another thing. In this declaration Mr. Ruez summed up all the materials, intercept materials that were received and requested by -- from the Bosnian authorities. I never saw in this material the binder of 550 pages that you mentioned. Could you tell me of a document which records the transfer of that binder?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot, off the top of my head, but I -- I believe that I can find a transfer document for you on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish the Prosecution to do that for you, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I would like very much to see that, because we haven't had an opportunity to see that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Vanderpuye, we will continue, but in the meantime, if you could kindly try and locate it. If -- if this document exists, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I will happily look into the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that the 550-page binder contained printed materials, but with no headings on the printed materials, they contained only the contents of reports without the headings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- yes, if I could explain just a little bit. It's partially true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 550 pages contained both material that was recorded by the police and by the military. The conversations that were recorded by the police had the standard heading on it that they put at the beginning of every conversation. You're familiar with those, I think, on the above-mentioned date at this and this time, this frequency we recorded, blah, blah, blah. The headings for the military -- the military -- let me go back. The headings on the conversations that were recorded by the military were not included in that set of -- in that collection of 550 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you did not have the military intercepts in the binder which contained 550 pages. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had the military intercepts as well. We just didn't have the headers for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Which means intercepts intercepted by the military were contained in the 550-page binder but without the headers?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me who handed that binder over to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, are we in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now. If we need to go in private session, we will do so for the mention of this person. If -- if you are going to mention anybody.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to check it. I may have been the person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we will remain in public session. In the meantime, during the break, if you have an opportunity of checking, perhaps you can go through your documents or records and then let us know after the break. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will go back to this question after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: For now I would like to ask you on another matter. You told us that these reports without the headers were an analytical tool, in essence, and that the headers were not included to facilitate analysis of that material. Am I right in interpreting your testimony in this way?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding was that the binder that we received was a compilation of the material that -- that 2 Corps was using.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any explanation why the headers were excluded from the materials?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the time we didn't even know there were headers on the material.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Judging by your experience, given your work with the BiH army and judging by the consultations with your colleagues who also were involved in investigation and analysis, would it be true if I said that the BiH army was organised and structured in accordance with the same principles as any other modern armed forces?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I'm qualified to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you answer a question whether, in the BiH army, there was a principle of subordination being observed? Simply put, a subordinate had to follow his superior's orders?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm not a military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You have not consulted any experts that you worked with about these questions that I am putting to you?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, I observed in meetings -- I mean, I understand ranks and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you don't know that a private is supposed to obey his superior's orders?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move, Mr. Zivanovic. Let's move, change the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to go back to the document, or the declaration by Mr. Ruez. In his declaration Mr. Ruez says that on several occasions the Tribunal in 1995, 1996, and 1997, and let's go back to page 1, please, while I'm saying this. Paragraph 3. So it says here that the Tribunal in 1995, 1996, 1997, addressed AID, requesting access of the intercepts and the reply was that the timing for handing over such materials was not right. First of all I would like to ask you whether you know what the acronym AID stands for. Could you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe -- with absolute certainty, not at this moment. I think it's [B/C/S spoken] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was not translated in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but I think we've heard before what the acronym stands for. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about that. You know what the acronym SDB stands for; I presume that you used to come across that acronym in the materials that were you given in the binder.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what the acronym stands for. Without looking at the material in the binder, I can't say for certain that that -- oh, well, yes, it might have been there next to a date. SDB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what this acronym stands for?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the State Security Services.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that after the war, after that service was renamed and that it was given the name, Agency for Research and Documentation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us take a look at Defence Exhibit 1D2818 -- 218. 1D218. This document has not been translated; we have it only in the B/C/S version. Could you please take a look at this document and tell me in -- in the header, if you could scroll up a bit, it says, "Ministry of the Interior." Then the state security sector, or the acronym SDB. Could you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the date, 24th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out the addressee, the army of the republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the 2nd Corps, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you read out or can you see the subject, "Fono documents being requested"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Though I don't know what "Fono" means.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Fono meaning audio. This is a synonym in BHS [as interpreted] for audio documents. And from this very brief text, one can tell that what is requested are audio tapes, so-called Fono documents, referring to Srebrenica. Given, and I quote the last offensive against the protected zone, and that this audio material is sought to prepare materials for the ICTY at -- is that correct? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see this memo, this document? In search of the intercepts, have you ever heard about the existence of such a request?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I presume that you do not know the reply that this memo elicited?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us take a look at 1D219. This document has not been translated either. Is this a document prepared by the General Staff of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the header, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this document, does it bear the date 19th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 18th of August, 1995, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it addressed to the 2nd Corps command?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a seal testifying to the receipt by the 2nd Corps command on the 19th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document request the handing over of materials for the "international court - instruction"? Is it stated in the document?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document refers to the previous document from the 24th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would want to compare the numbers, but by the date and -- and that -- it appears to, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether we can juxtapose those two documents, the previous one and this one for the purpose of you comparing the references or the numbers. If it's possible, I have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there contestation from the Prosecution that the reference is to the previous document that we saw?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The microphones don't seem to work. If I speak loudly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can do nothing about it, Mr. Vanderpuye. I can see you are pushing all kinds of buttons. If I hear what you say I can repeat it and we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There is no objection to the juxtaposition of the two documents; however, I do have an objection to the relevancy, only to the extent that I think that my esteemed colleague is implying that this is a response to the prior letter which the witness testified she wasn't aware of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, I don't think he said that it was a response. He said it is a further letter, as I understood his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I withdraw the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can safely take it that the reference is to the previous letter that we saw on the screen a few minutes ago. So we would rather not lose time. Let's proceed. The date was certainly the 24th, 7, 1995, and the [B/C/S spoken] [No interpretation], it's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And in the last two rows of this memo, does the Main Staff of the BiH army request from the 2nd Corps command to hand over those materials to the SDB sector of Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Okay. Is the entire letter on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Frease.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Reading all these intercepts you mentioned that on numerous occasions it was stated that they were sent to the intelligence organ of the 2nd Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I've just been told by my colleagues is that the previous document, if you could read it, it's a very brief one, and since it has not been translated, let's help those who do not read B/C/S. Maybe I can read it out loud and you confirm it or you can read it out aloud, whichever way it's easier for you. Would you like me to read it out aloud and you can confirm it? "Through the SDB Sarajevo MUP we've been informed that the SDB Tuzla, through its document 7-1022, dated 24th of July, 1995, requested from you audio recordings that refer to the events connected with Srebrenica. Given that the requested audio recordings are of very great importance of the dossier which is being collated for the international war crimes court, it is necessary for these materials to be handed over to the SDB sector of Tuzla." Is this what it is stated in this document?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In a great number of printed materials and documents that you received, and I'm going back to what I started asking questions about, you saw that they were addressed to the intelligence organ of the 2nd Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Previously I said yes. I would -- I would rather be able to look at one of the headings of one of the documents to see whether it specifically says the intelligence organ, but certainly, yes, they were -- they were addressed to 2 Corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You took all that over from the intelligence organ of the 2nd Corps. Would that be fair to say? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please look at 1D220. Is this another letter -- I apologise, can you scroll up a little to show the heading? Is this a letter drafted by the command of the 2nd Corps and does it bear the date of 24 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, a request was made to hand over audio recordings relative to Srebrenica to be used by the SDP [as interpreted] of Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a very faint copy, but it -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the text, we are not going to read it together, a reference is made to the previous two letters and a request is made that the audio materials should be forwarded to the state security department of Tuzla. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The copy is very faint on the screen for me. Are you looking -- can you tell me where you're looking? Okay. Right at the beginning of the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You can look at the very beginning of the letter, the first paragraph, or even the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that again a same -- the same request was made on the 24th of August, 1995, and that the request refers to the audio materials?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I now look at 1D221.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just see the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 1D221, please. Is this a letter that was drafted by the general staff of the BiH army on the 7th of July, 1996?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1997 of July, 1996, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 7th of July, 1996. And it was sent by the Ministry of the Interior of the Federation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the first paragraph of the letter? I'm going to read it out aloud and you tell me -- I believe that the letter was actually translated into English, that there -- I believe that there is an English translation of the document. I have been able to locate it on the EDS system. Don't you have it? No. Okay, I'm going to read the first paragraph and then you can tell me whether it is correct or not. "Pursuant to your request we have examined and verified a large portion of the collected information relative to the period of the occupation of Srebrenica and Zepa. We have established that all -- which aggressive forces participated in the occupation and the crimes that were committed. We have also established the names of the persons who in any way were engaged in the operations of the occupation, either through direct command or direct participation. In addition to the names of person we have also been able to establish information that we are privy to about their participation and the type of engagement. Most of the information was collected through electronic reconnaissance and all the audio documents were submitted earlier, as early as 1995 at the request to the agency for research and documentation of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina so that the intelligence service of the Main Staff of the BiH army does not possess the original documents that might serve as a valid proof in a possible trial." Have you ever seen the document?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The answer was no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you showed us -- actually, in your previous testimony you said that for the analysis of the intercepts that had been placed at your disposal you had used various sources, among which you used information that you received from various sources from other countries, from the photos, aerial photos, and I suppose that you received some information from the BiH army. Could you please be more precise and tell us what sources did you use when you analysed the intercepted conversations?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't use any sources from the BiH army. It -- I used sources -- this is off the top of my head, but to the best of my recollection I used video footage that was taken during the time of events by VRS cameramen and by Zoran Petrovic. Aerial imagery that was provided to the Court by the United States, letters that were provided to the Tribunal by UNPROFOR command, so from UN headquarters. Military documents that were seized in Zvornik, at Zvornik Brigade headquarters. And military documents that were obtained from the VRS Ministry of Defence. Those are the ones that I can remember right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you used aerial imagery that you received from the United States, can you tell us whether you are talking only about a video footage or are you also referring to some audio recordings?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No audio recordings, and when I say "aerial imagery," it's from the air, not video footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you didn't use information or documentation that originated from the BiH army. Did I understand you well? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why? Why did they not want to provide you with information about the Republika Srpska army or was there any other reason for that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we thought it would be much more objective if we could go to outside parties. Or to have corroboration from VRS documents themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that you had your reservations about any documentation that might have been provided to you by the BiH army, that ...

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that you first had to look at their documents in order to be able to draw a conclusion that it was not what you needed?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was never -- there was never an issue really of -- of including BiH documents in trying to corroborate the intercepts. The intercepts had been provided by the -- by the Bosnian authorities, and it was those intercepts in particular that we were trying to corroborate, so we didn't want to use anything that was associated with the BiH in order to corroborate material that they had provided to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, we will have a break in about three minutes' time. Mr. Zivanovic, sorry. I mean I keep ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can have our break straight away, as far as I'm concerned, if that's okay with the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The reason why I asked you is that I sensed we were coming to that. So we will have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you. And my apologies to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will continue where I left it off before the break. You have told us that you did not use any material on the Republika Srpska army that would have been provided to you by the BiH army when you carried out your analysis. Is that a fair representation of what you said?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that your personal position, or was it a position of the investigative team of the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority of the information that we had from BiH authorities actually -- well, didn't come from the authorities themselves, but from witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My question was very specific. I'm not talking about the authorities, I'm talking about the BiH army. My question was this: Did you receive information about the army of Republika Srpska that was in the possession of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received some information at a certain point. I don't remember exactly when. I think it was -- could have been in May of 1999. But it wasn't considered relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you consider it reliable?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard for me to talk about it in sort of very general terms. One -- one things that comes to mind is some tactical intercepts that we had received as well that we simply weren't able to confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My question did not refer to the intercepted information, but other information that the BiH army might have had about the Republika Srpska army as their opponent, as their enemy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. The -- I do object to the question to the extent that it doesn't identify the specific information that my colleague has put to the witness. I think the witness has answered the question to the best of her ability. She has indicated a general response to a rather general question. I think if there is specific information my colleague wants -- wishes to inquire about, he should perhaps put that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you have to say about that, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that, and I will move on to another more specific question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at 1D222. Again we don't have an English translation. Can we together confirm that this document was drafted by the joint command of the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that the date on the document is the 3rd of March, 1998?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we also confirm that this document was sent to Mr. Jean-Rene Ruez, who was the leader of the investigation team?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a list of the collected material and documents that were being handed over to the investigation team of the international tribunal in The Hague? Does this transpire from the first three lines in the body of this text? A list of the collected material and documents that are being handed over to the investigation team of the international criminal tribunal in The Hague? I apologise. I did not hear your answer, so I have repeated the question, which probably wasn't necessary. Does it continue to say in this letter that pursuant to an order of the commander of the joint command of the army of the Federation dated 16 February 1998 at a request of the Prosecutor's office of the international criminal tribunal in The Hague reports that were collected by radio reconnaissance are being handed over as well as the information on the organisation and formation structure of the Drina Corps of the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And your previous question also yes. I had been looking at a different part of the document so I wasn't following what you were saying. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We may then say that two things were handed over on that occasion. Reports collected by radio reconnaissance, as well as the organisational information structure of the Republika Srpska army, Drina Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we move on to the next page of this document, please? The next page is the organisation and formation structure of the Drina Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we move on to the following page, please?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, on the transcript the answer was yes. And then the question was, "Can we move on to the following page, please?" Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the top of the page do you see a box with the abbreviation DK?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this stand for the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read on the bullet one on the left side of the page what does it say there? Or maybe I can try and read it. It says, "Zvornicka MBR," which is the abbreviation for the motorised brigade, so it is the Zvornik Motorised Brigade isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Again, I mean, I'm not a military expert, so I can help as much as I can, but I think I will be limited in what I can help you with here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think you will need any expert knowledge for this. Again under 2 it says Zvornik RLPBR [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that you don't know that the abbreviation that you see here stands for a light infantry brigade?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We may then conclude that there were two Zvornik Brigades. Wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. We're asking the witness to speculate on matters outside the subject of her direct examination. We could literally go through and spend weeks, if he's throwing up documents like this, without any tying, he is not putting his case to the witness. I just -- we're going nowhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's your comment on that, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My comment is that the witness explained to us that she was involved in analysis based on various sources, and it arises from this document that these documents were given to the investigation team that was led by Mr. Ruez, and that these documents should have been used when radio reports were being handed over, accompanied by this letter. On the other hand, these radio reports that were submitted with the documents do not exist in any file, in any binder, not even in the statement provided by Mr. Ruez. You know that my general position is that I am contesting the authenticity and the reliability of all the materials that were obtained through radio surveillance, and in that sense I believe that my question is relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your question was, we may conclude that there were two Zvornik Brigades. Wouldn't that be correct. The previous one is also related to abbreviations standing for light infantry brigade. Anyway, let's confer a little bit amongst ourselves, please, before we decide this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we agree with the position taken or the objection raised by Mr. McCloskey. I mean that's the caveat. If you wish to put a direct question, you are in cross-examination in any case to the witness, whether she's made use of these documents, then obviously you are free to put such questions. On the other hand, on these military issues she has already told you that basically she knows what the ranks were, and that's about it. She doesn't know much more. So -- yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have a question with regards to the procedure, maybe we can shed some light on this. Mr. McCloskey is not the person who was examining. I do not oppose to this, but I would like to know if the same principle is applied to the Defence, basically. He is not the person who led the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I remember well, and my memory doesn't fail me, Madam Fauveau, this rose up with Maitre de Roux and Maitre Pitron in Brdjanin when they had a habit of both standing up, you included, and I said either one or none. So she saw Mr. De Roux yesterday and that must have revived her memory. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and I -- I agree with that, I think we have to try to do that. Obviously otherwise it would be impossible. On the other hand, I am the only one from the Prosecution is here day in and day out and sees the bigger picture. I have also been here since 1996 so I can see these documents and see how they relate or don't relate to the intercepts. And so while I try to keep my mouth as quiet as possible when other people are here, I -- I really sometimes I just will -- will object, and I -- I try to keep that to a minimum because I -- I agree with that, that's an important rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you had come from my region, I would have attributed it to Mediterranean temper, Mr. McCloskey. Anyway, if we could avoid such interjections, however, I think that should be the rule that we ought to follow. And you can ask -- ask to stop for a moment, you can confer with Mr. Vanderpuye, who is more than capable of then transmitting the objection to us and to the rest. So I apologise to you, Mr. Zivanovic, for that interruption. Please proceed in accordance to the direction that we gave you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the first page of this document you saw that reports on radio surveillance were handed over to Mr. Ruez. Did you see those reports ever?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to know which reports you're referring to. It could be -- well, I would rather not speculate. I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't want to speculate either, but I don't have any other information except for what I read from page 1, so I cannot say anything else. But let's go through the document page by page to see whether radio surveillance is mentioned anywhere. This document is 20 page long, we can go page by page. I contest that there are no mentions of radio surveillance reports, and if the Prosecution stipulates, then we can drop this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. It's rather complicated, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think it is. I don't know if it might be just a better question to put to the witness whether she's seen this document before and that might solve the issue right quick, as they say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a pertinent remark. Mr. Zivanovic, I suggest you put that question first to the witness. Of course she might be familiar with the document or she might not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to hand over this document to the witness - its hard copy - to take a look at it, and to tell us whether it is the document in question and whether it makes mention of radio surveillance reports at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This idea of -- this idea of having the witness read through a document which is not hers, which she may not have seen before, and asking her to go through it and reply or state whether it makes mention of a particular subject matter, I mean it's -- it's a procedure to which I am completely not only unused, but not familiar, but alien, completely alien. If you intend to make use of this document if you intend to tender it, it speaks for itself and then you put the question to either the person who can give us explanations on the document, but why this particular witness? I mean, if the document doesn't mention for example intercepts, and it's a 20-page document, why should we spend I don't know how many minutes for the witness to go through the entire 20 pages and then to confirm what appears on the face of document itself? I mean, I don't know. I'm not used to that kind of -- I haven't conferred with my colleagues on -- on this, so I stand to be corrected, but I think it would be a mere waste of time. Let me confer with my colleagues first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Our suggestion is, let's start first, you ask -- you put the question to the witness whether she's familiar with this document, whether she's seen it before, and then we see which way to proceed. But, please, let's not waste time. Go ahead, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like just to ask the witness whether, after March the 3rd, she received from Mr. Ruez any radio reports by which I mean radio intercepts. Because witness was in charge of that material within the investigation team, and this document refers to the handing over of the radio surveillance reports and the organisation and the structure of the Drina Corps, and this is something that she ought to be in a position to answer, of course if she knows that, and this is the gist of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a completely different question. We are talking of a document. First we need to establish whether she is familiar with the document, whether she has seen it before. You don't -- anyway, let's start with that first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall having seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you can move to your next question, please, but not asking the witness what the document contains or does not contain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not going ask that. I wanted to ask something else, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive from Mr. Ruez any radio intercepts after the 3rd of March, 1998?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is related to a previous subject that we talked about, which was when did we receive the binder of 550 intercepts. I believe that we received those in March, but I -- I really need to check documents to be able to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I understood you as saying that you received that in April 1998 and it was received by Mr. Peter Nicholson as far as I can recall this was your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look at documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me broach another subject of the notebooks. Were you present when the notebooks were listed on the 11th of March, 1998?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not to my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You took over those notebooks on the 24th of April, 1998. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, on that occasion, leaf through or read what was in the notebooks?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I leafed through some, as far as I recall, but I didn't read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was the choice of those to be leafed through was random or did you have any instructions that guided your selection of which are going to be leafed through?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The selection had already been made. It was made in March when the notebooks were first discovered. And then they were put in a box and sealed. When I returned, when I went to Tuzla in April I picked up those notebooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about the choice of the notebooks that you are going to read and not selection of the notebooks that would be taken by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you went through some notebooks, that you did not read them out, you just leafed through them, took a look at them. As I am -- am I correct in saying that you said that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So my question is, was the choice random, the selection of the notebooks that you are going to leaf through or go through?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In those notebooks did you notice any corrections being made, maybe another figure being written instead of a pre-existing figure or something like that? Did you notice such interventions in those notebooks?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me to say nine years, you know -- nine years have passed since -- since that happened. They were certainly working documents, and I did notice that different ink was used in the notebooks, but I don't have specific recollections of specific mark -- you know, cross-outs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the date when you took over those notebooks on the 24th of April, but later on when you had ample time to peruse them, I believe in priming yourself for this testimony, you did so, and did you notice any corrections to the dates or names or frequencies or any other modifications using different inks or different longhand, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Once the notebooks were in our possession, we had an opportunity to go through and to log all of the notebooks. To go through and to note the dates that were contained within the notebooks, to have a quick look -- to also note the names that were contained within the notebooks, to provide us a guide, to know how to approach the analytical part of extracting the information from the relevant notebooks. And, yes, during that analysis I noticed cross-outs, different types of ink used, different handwritings in the -- in the notebook. As I said, they were clearly working documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My question being, did you try to establish or check when these modifications took place?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at two notebooks, I believe it's possible to do so by placing it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Let me stop you for a moment, Mr. Zivanovic, so that I will try to clear this up a little bit better. His question was: "My question being, did you try to establish and check when these modifications took place." Your answer was no. Do I take it that in the process of your work analysis you did discuss these corrections, modifications, with any of the operators that you may have had contact with, or that you never discussed the -- these modifications or alterations on the notebooks with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We talked about the modifications with the operators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And could you come to a conclusion? And if yes, what was that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That they would -- that they made corrections as they went along. If they replayed the tape and could hear things better and could correct the record, their transcription, then they made those changes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you believe such explanations given by the operators?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you double-check in any way these claims?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only among the various operators. Not with an outside handwriting expert, for example, though, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the two notebooks that I asked to be placed on the ELMO. P22308 [as interpreted] and 2322.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So for the record, the transcript shows P22308, it's P2308, if I heard Mr. Zivanovic correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2308. [In English] That's correct. [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 2308 notebook, please turn at page 9685, 0779685. Can we confirm that there was a modification to the channel?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Otherwise, can you tell the time, 11515 [as interpreted], and that the frequency was 785000?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the other notebook, 2322. Page 0784. Place it a bit lower, please. Or lift it up. Can you see the same frequency in this other notebook, but now it's third channel and the time has been altered also?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that the time has been altered. I think they just drew a line through the zeros for 10.05 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why wouldn't the other three zeros behind 785 be crossed like that as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I stand to be corrected, but the first one across the first zero isn't just a straight line, it looks like a one with -- with the tail or whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. If I could just refer to the other page, there's a marking through the zero three on the channel. Here. And yet no -- no marking through the zero on the -- on the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I take your point. Yeah. Okay. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you believe that in this case there was no alteration or correction, but could you tell me what was the time when this intercept was transcribed?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this I would say 10.05, but I would -- I would double-check it at this point, since we have the opportunity to double-check. I would double-check it and cross-reference it against the electronic copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, could these alterations influence the authenticity of these transcripts? In one case we have a different channel; instead of a channel 3 now it's channel 5. If you go back to the previous notebook the first entry that you had to look at. And so if you were to align these two entries, then you would have the same channel, same frequencies, and same time, and recording of two different conversations at the same time. Would that, in your opinion, influence the authenticity of what was transcribed here?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there are just too many hypotheticals in what you have asked. So I would -- yeah, I mean I -- I would check more. Against the -- against the hard copy records to see, but in principle I -- I would say, no, that this -- this wouldn't affect, you know, the reliability.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You -- thank you. I no longer need these notebooks. Among other things, you stated that the notebooks were recorded in the corps command before handed over to units that would transcribe intercepts, that they would be given a registration number, and that that registration would be dated. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that those numbers were registered. They were registered by the captain, and I believe that they were registered at the corps headquarters, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
